content: Nafcillin and aspirin (rectal) can increase each other's levels due to competition for plasma protein binding. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Nafcillin and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Close monitoring is necessary. Nafcillin decreases the therapeutic effects of atezolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are required. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of atogepant by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The recommended atogepant dosage with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is 30 mg or 60 mg once daily. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin reduces the therapeutic effects of avelumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. Alternative therapy is recommended. Nafcillin decreases the levels of axitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Select medications with minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. Azithromycin reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Close monitoring is advised. Nafcillin reduces the effects of balstilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. Close monitoring is necessary. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral hormone forms. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nafcillin reduces the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. Coadministration is contraindicated. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced therapeutic efficacy. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of belumosudil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Nafcillin and bendroflumethiazide can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Nafcillin decreases the levels of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce bosutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 85%. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce brigatinib efficacy. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of buprenorphine (all formulations, including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For subdermal implants, monitor for withdrawal symptoms, and consider implant removal if necessary. For long-acting injections, ensure adequate plasma levels and transition to an adjustable dosage form if needed. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Alternative therapy is recommended. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer is required, increase the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the inducer. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Drugs that stimulate microsomal hydroxylation reduce the half-life of calcifediol. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin decreases the effects of camrelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. Close monitoring is necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider increasing the cannabidiol dosage based on clinical response and tolerability. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers reduce capivasertib exposure, potentially decreasing efficacy. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of capmatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration is contraindicated. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites. The effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure has not been evaluated, and the net effect is unclear. Nafcillin reduces the effects of cemiplimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. Alternative therapy is recommended. Nafcillin decreases the levels of ceritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. Chloramphenicol reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Close monitoring is advised. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Chlorothiazide increases nafcillin levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. Nafcillin reduces the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Nafcillin and choline magnesium trisalicylate can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of citalopram by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Close monitoring is advised. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of clonazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of clorazepate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may reduce cobimetinib systemic exposure by over 80%, decreasing efficacy. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin decreases the effects of cosibelimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. Close monitoring is necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of crizotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of darifenacin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may increase the metabolism of CYP3A4 substrates. Close monitoring is necessary. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. Alternative therapy is recommended. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal and intranasal) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the rate of diazepam elimination, reducing its efficacy. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on strong CYP3A4 inducers. This combination should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuing the inducer. Nafcillin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora.
